newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Demand, capacity boosts Pannonplast H1.
newsitem.headline: Demand, capacity boosts Pannonplast H1.

text.p: Hungarian plastics industrial group Pannonplast reported rising earnings for the first half of 1997, saying it benefited from stronger demand for certain products and higher capacity.

"The major driving force was the increased demand on the markets for packaging materials and infrastructure-related products, as well as new capacity because of the company's investments and acquisitions," Pannonplast said on Friday.
Pannonplast reported an IAS consolidated net income of 910 million forints for the first six months of 1997, compared to 668 million in the same period of 1996.

The group boosted the proportion of exports within total sales to 32.9 percent from 30 percent, as its exports rose by 72 percent, faster than its total sales which rose 57 percent to 6.556 billion forints from 4.177 billion.

Pannonplast spent 763 million forints for acquisitions and for purchasing ownership stakes and spent 642 million forints to raise the capital of its group members to increase capacity and widen product range.
